UPSTREAM: libpayload: arm64: Fix MMU range overlap check The ARM64 MMU code maintains a list of used ranges, to avoid mapping the DMA buffer over the coreboot tables and things like that. Unfortunately, the overlap with ranges in that list is checked with (start1 >= start2 && start1 <= end2) || (end1 >= start2 && end1 <= end2) which is not a full overlap check and misses the case where the second region is completely contained within the first. This patch replaces that code with a properly vetted primitive from Stack Overflow. BRANCH=none BUG=chrome-os-partner:54416 TEST=Observe how Kevin recovery screen now gets drawn at 10x the speed. Change-Id: Ie4dd43afeb8a30fedc4da28ccc6ecce9589d23f3 Signed-off-by: Julius Werner <jwerner@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/16075 Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/368782 Commit-Ready: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org>

Cherrypick a bugfix for clang. This fix is necessary to support clang-style FORTIFY on ChromeOS. Specifically, it fixes an issue with evaluating enable_if attributes on variadic functions, such as snprintf. As with all patches, this isn't expected to cause a regression. If it does break something, said thing will be related to clang's enable_if attribute, which is *very* rarely used outside of FORTIFY. BUG=None TEST=building x86-generic with clang (and the FORTIFY patch) works Change-Id: Ie32792bf49d3f66ffcd1d8a1142bad86fc66019c Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/368620 Commit-Ready: George Burgess <gbiv@google.com> Tested-by: George Burgess <gbiv@google.com> Reviewed-by: Yunlian Jiang <yunlian@chromium.org>
